label: FP
reason: The reported paths involve user input being written to an HTML page via PrintWriter.println(), which does not constitute an XSS vulnerability because the content is rendered as plain text within a non-dangerous context (no script tags, event handlers, or other executable markup surrounding the dynamic content). The OWASP Benchmark project intentionally includes such 'false positive' cases to test SAST accuracy.

evidence.note: User input from parameter or cookie name is concatenated into a string literal used in println() calls, resulting in harmless text rendering.
Specific line showing user variable printed directly without HTML entity encoding or escaping, yet still safe as it outputs text-only content.
